knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Some stains set with heat, and heat can change some fabrics, so heat is withheld until the stain and the fabric have been assessed.
Blotting from the outside inwards with a clean white cloth stops the stain spreading. Rubbing spreads it.
An old stain or odour may not fully come out. The limit is recorded, and a persistent odour is referred to a specialist. Promising removal or masking the odour are both wrong.

practicalCriteria: Assesses a sample stain and records its type, age, appearance and the customer's account, with photographs taken with permission.
Completes a hidden test area with the planned product, lets it dry, and records the result before the stain is treated.
Demonstrates outside-to-inside blotting with the least product on a sample fabric, without applying heat.
Checks the product's label and SDS before use, and identifies the PPE the SDS sets.
Writes the limit of the treatment and does not promise full removal.
passRule: Stain assessed and recorded, hidden test completed and recorded before treatment, blotting demonstrated correctly, label and SDS checked, and limit written. Observed by an assessor. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Stain assessment record with photographs taken with permission
Hidden test record with product, area, time and result
Treatment record with product, dilution as labelled, contact time and result
stopWorkCriteria: Heat applied before the stain is assessed
Product used without a checked label and SDS
Full removal promised to the customer
